drafted_from: tool row in tools/compare-voice-and-music-models/tool-rows.json, do-work/render_note_events.py (run for real) and tools/compare-voice-and-music-models/test/test_compare_models.py
start_here: Say to your AI: "Render the note events in events.json to playback.wav so I can measure what the transcription model wrote down."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads one JSON file of note events and writes one WAV.
instructions: 1. Have events.json: a list of {type: start, pitch, start_time, index?}, {type: end, start_event_index, end_time} and {type: drum, start_time}.

2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads this tool's row with tools:list {tool: "tool:render-music-note-events-to-a-test-wav"}, installs numpy and soundfile if missing and runs the command in given.
3. Read the last line: {"result": {wav, seconds, events, sample_rate}}. The same events always give the same file.
4. Measure playback.wav beside the original with your audio meter; it is a test rendering, never music to use.

worked_examples.title: An A440 note, a drum hit and an unfinished note become 3.2 seconds of audio
worked_examples.ask: Turn these note events into a WAV I can measure.
worked_examples.given: From tools/compare-voice-and-music-models/test/test_compare_models.py (RenderNoteEvents.test_a_note_and_a_drum_become_a_stereo_wav_one_second_past_the_last_note), run for real. events.json = [{"type":"start","pitch":69,"start_time":0.0,"index":0},{"type":"drum","start_time":1.0},{"type":"end","start_event_index":0,"end_time":0.5},{"type":"start","pitch":81,"start_time":2.0}]. Run: python3 -I tools/compare-voice-and-music-models/do-work/render_note_events.py events.json playback.wav
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result":{"wav":"playback.wav","seconds":3.2,"events":3,"sample_rate":48000}}: a 48 kHz 24-bit stereo WAV peaking at half scale; the MIDI 69 note is 440 Hz in the first half second, the drum sounds at 1 s, and the last note (no end event) lasts 0.2 s by the length rule, so 2.2 + 1.0 = 3.2 s. With only one argument it answers {"error":"pass <events.json> <out.wav>"} (exit 2).
